story.iWant: to understand how the bootloader uses QSPI and memory resources
story.soThat: I can design a safe state persistence mechanism that doesn't conflict with bootloader operations
story.tasks: - Research Daisy bootloader documentation and source code (AC: #1, #2) - Locate bootloader version and source - Document bootloader QSPI usage - Analyze QSPI memory layout (AC: #2, #6) - Map bootloader reserved regions - Identify safe application regions - Determine bootloader timing requirements (AC: #3, #4) - Measure bootloader execution time - Specify safe delay value - Document root cause analysis (AC: #5, #7) - Explain state corruption mechanism - Document SD card/QSPI interactions

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: - Bootloader version, source location, and behavior documented - QSPI memory layout identified with specific addresses (bootloader region, firmware region, safe application region) - Bootloader execution timeline documented with timing values - Minimum required delay before QSPI access determined (e.g., 100ms) - Root cause of state corruption identified and explained - Safe QSPI address range specified for PersistentStorage - Any SD card loading interference with QSPI documented
